Conventions

This reference is generated from the server's OpenAPI 3.1 description, openapi.yaml, which you can load into any OpenAPI tool or client generator. Paths are relative to wherever the server is reachable: its host and port, or a reverse proxy in front of it. The port is 10111 unless changed with LOWKEY_PORT or the port config key.

Each endpoint lists its access level, parameters, request body and responses with every field's type. A type name such as Job links to its definition under Schemas. Bodies are JSON unless a content type says otherwise. Booleans in query strings are the literal strings true and false. A path parameter written {id} is one path segment.

Many older handlers do not check the HTTP method and accept any method with the documented body; the method shown is the one the clients send. Where it matters, the endpoint says so.

Code is coloured by role: literal --flag {param} /path ENV_VAR "value" { }

Access Levels

Every endpoint is marked with one of three access levels.

LevelRequirement
PublicNo credential.
ReadA credential, unless the allowPublicAccess setting is on, in which case anonymous requests are accepted. Write methods on a Read path still require a credential while public access is on; the endpoint notes this.
AdminA credential. Every authenticated user is an admin.

A credential is one of: an Authorization: Bearer <token> header carrying a JWT or an lk_ API key; an X-API-Key: <key> header; or the auth_token cookie set by POST /auth/login. Headers are checked before the cookie. JWTs and the cookie are valid for one year; API keys until revoked.

A request that fails authentication receives 401 when it carries a Bearer or X-API-Key header, sends exactly Accept: application/json, or targets a path under /api/. Any other request is redirected with 302: to /setup until first-run setup is complete, then to /login.

While the temporary default admin account is the only user, requests authenticated as it receive 403 with {"error": "setup_required", "message": "Please create a new user account"}; page requests are redirected to /login?setup=true.

Errors

There is no single error envelope. Most handlers write {"error": "<message>"} (the Error schema), often labelled Content-Type: text/plain because they go through Go's http.Error; parse the body as JSON regardless of the header. Older handlers write a bare plain-text message. Each endpoint lists the statuses it returns and which form the body takes. The status codes follow HTTP semantics:

StatusMeaning
400Malformed JSON, a missing required field, an invalid parameter, or a failed validation.
401Missing or invalid credential (see above).
403Path outside every configured storage root, setup required, or a cross-origin form post.
404Unknown job, workflow, model, file, person, or scene.
405Method not supported, on handlers that check the method.
409Conflict: a move destination already in the library, a tag in another category.
413Request body over its cap.
422The input was valid but unusable, for example an image with no face to search by.
500Database or filesystem failure.
503A subsystem is unavailable: the auto scheduler is not running, or the event stream is at its connection limit.

Media Paths

A media item is identified by its path: the absolute filesystem path for local roots, or s3://bucket/key for object storage roots. Paths are compared as stored. Endpoints that serve or process a file refuse paths outside every configured storage root with 403. Paths in query strings must be URL-encoded.

Platform Differences

The Windows, macOS and Linux servers register the same routes with the same access levels, with these exceptions:

  • POST /api/embedding/directml/install and the /events page exist only on Windows.
  • The /stats page exists only on macOS and Linux.
  • GET /tasks includes each task's options only on Windows.
  • POST /api/upload honours the destination field only on Windows; macOS and Linux always write to uploads/ in the default root.
  • /api/scene-dream endpoints exist only in builds made with the Dream feature (LOKI_DREAM=1).

Authentication

Every non-public route runs through the server's auth middleware. A request is authenticated by one of these credentials, checked in this order:

  • an X-API-Key: lk_... header;
  • an Authorization: Bearer <token> header carrying either a JWT (from POST /auth/login) or an lk_ API key (anything starting with lk_ is checked against the API-key table, anything else as a JWT);
  • the auth_token cookie set by POST /auth/login (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, expires with the JWT after 365 days).

A header credential that fails verification is not fatal by itself: the middleware falls through to the cookie. When nothing valid is found the response depends on the kind of request. It is treated as an API request, and answered 401 with the plain-text body Unauthorized, when any of these is true: the Accept header is exactly application/json, the request carries an X-API-Key or Bearer header, or the path starts with /api/. Every other request (a browser navigation) gets a 302 redirect to /login?redirect=<original URI>, or to /setup while first-run setup is not complete.

Before first-run setup, the server has a temporary admin/admin account. While that is the only account, a request authenticated as it is refused: API requests get 403 with the JSON body {"error":"setup_required","message":"Please create a new user account"}; page requests are redirected to /login?setup=true (or /setup). Creating the first real user (POST /auth/users or the setup wizard) deletes the temporary account.

Access levels on each operation (x-access): public needs no credential; read needs one unless Allow Public Access (allowPublicAccess in the config) is on, in which case anonymous requests pass, but write methods on mixed routes still require a credential and answer 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} without one; admin always needs a credential. Every authenticated user is an admin.

API keys live in the library database, so switching the server to another database (POST /config with a new dbPath) makes existing keys and sessions invalid there.

POST/auth/loginPublic#

Exchange a username and password for a JWT.

On success the JWT is returned in the body and also set as the auth_token cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, expiring after 365 days, the same lifetime as the token). CORS on this route echoes a chrome-extension:// or moz-extension:// origin, otherwise allows http://localhost:1212, with credentials. OPTIONS answers 200 with no body.

Request body

application/json

usernamestring
passwordstring
Example
{
"username": "alice",
"password": "correct-horse"
}

Response 200

Logged in.

application/json

statusstringrequired

One of "ok".

tokenstringrequired

The JWT. Use it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

setup_requiredbooleanrequired

True when the login used the temporary admin account and it is still the only account. Requests made with this token are refused until a real user is created.

Example
{
"status": "ok",
"token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...",
"setup_required": false
}

Errors

  • 400Body is not valid JSON. Plain text Invalid JSON. text/plain
  • 401Wrong username or password (or a database error during lookup). The body is the text {"error":"Invalid credentials"} sent with a text/plain content type. text/plain
  • 405Method other than POST or OPTIONS. Plain text. text/plain
POST/auth/logoutPublic#

Clear the session cookie.

Expires the auth_token cookie. It does not revoke the JWT itself: a copy of the token held elsewhere stays valid until it expires. Any method other than POST and OPTIONS (for example a browser GET /auth/logout) clears the cookie and answers 302 to /login.

Response 200

Cookie cleared.

application/json

statusstringrequired

One of "ok".

Response 302

Returned for non-POST methods. Redirects to /login.

GET/auth/statusPublic#

Report whether the request carries a valid credential.

Never fails: an invalid credential reports loggedIn: false. Header credentials are checked first. When the credential is the auth_token cookie, the response also carries the session's JWT in token, so the embedded web viewer can use it as a Bearer token. The handler does not check the method; every method except OPTIONS behaves like GET.

Response 200

Credential status.

application/json

loggedInbooleanrequired
usernamestring

Present when loggedIn is true.

publicAccessbooleanrequired

Whether Allow Public Access is on.

defaultStartPathstring

The configured default start path for the viewer. Present when loggedIn is true.

tokenstring

The cookie session's JWT. Present only when the credential was the cookie.

Example
{
"loggedIn": true,
"username": "alice",
"publicAccess": false,
"defaultStartPath": "D:\\Media"
}

POST/auth/usersPublic#

Create a user account.

Open without a credential only while setup is required (the temporary admin account is the only account). After that the caller must present a valid credential (header or cookie). Creating a user also deletes the temporary admin account if it still exists. The username admin is reserved.

Created. The body is {"status":"created"} (no Content-Type header is set).

One of "created".

Errors

  • 403Setup is complete and the request has no valid credential. Body is the text {"error":"unauthorized"} with a text/plain content type. text/plain

GET/auth/cli/authorizePublic#

Browser approval page for the CLI loopback login flow.

Step 1 of the RFC 8252 loopback flow with PKCE used by lokictl login and the viewer's "Sign in with browser". The client listens on 127.0.0.1:<port>, generates a PKCE verifier and opens this page. Only the auth_token cookie session counts here (header credentials are ignored). With no session the browser is redirected to /login?redirect=<this URL>. The page shows the key name and user, and posts the same parameters back to this URL with action=approve or action=deny.

Query parameters

portintegerrequired

Loopback port the client listens on.

min 1, max 65535.

statestringrequired

Opaque client state, echoed back on the callback.

code_challengestringrequired

base64url (no padding) SHA-256 of the PKCE verifier (S256).

namestring

Name for the API key that will be minted. Control characters are stripped; truncated to 64 bytes.

Default "lokictl".

Response 200

The approval page (Cache-Control: no-store).

text/html

string

Response 302

No browser session. Redirects to /login?redirect=....

Errors

  • 400invalid port, invalid state or invalid code_challenge. Plain text. text/plain
  • 403The session belongs to the temporary admin account. Plain text. text/plain
POST/auth/cli/authorizePublic#

Approve or deny the CLI login and redirect to the loopback callback.

Submitted by the approval page. The redirect target is always built server-side as http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback. On approve, a one-time authorization code bound to the session user, the PKCE challenge and the key name is minted (single use, expires after 2 minutes) and the browser is sent to ...callback?code=<code>&state=<state>. On deny (any action other than approve), it is sent to ...callback?error=access_denied&state=<state>. If the browser sends an Origin header, its host must equal the request Host.

Request body

application/x-www-form-urlencoded

portintegerrequired

min 1, max 65535.

statestringrequired
code_challengestringrequired
namestring

Default "lokictl".

actionstringrequired

One of "approve" "deny".

Response 303

Redirect to the loopback callback with code and state, or error=access_denied and state.

Errors

  • 400Unparseable form or invalid port/state/code_challenge. Plain text. text/plain
  • 401Approve without a valid auth_token cookie. Plain text Not logged in. text/plain
  • 403Cross-origin post, or the session is the temporary admin account. Plain text. text/plain
  • 500Could not create the code. Plain text. text/plain
POST/auth/cli/tokenPublic#

Exchange a CLI authorization code and PKCE verifier for a new API key.

Step 2 of the loopback flow. The code is consumed on the first attempt whether or not the verifier matches. On success a new lk_ API key is minted for the approving user, named after the name given to the authorize page.

Request body

application/json

codestringrequired

The code from the callback.

code_verifierstringrequired

PKCE verifier; SHA-256 of it, base64url-encoded without padding, must equal the code_challenge.

Example
{
"code": "9f2c...e1",
"code_verifier": "dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk"
}

Response 200

Key minted.

application/json

statusstringrequired

One of "ok".

keystringrequired

The plaintext lk_ API key.

usernamestringrequired
namestringrequired

The key's name.

Example
{
"status": "ok",
"key": "lk_ab12cd34...",
"username": "alice",
"name": "lokictl@host"
}

Errors

  • 400Invalid JSON, Invalid code_verifier, Invalid or expired code, or code_verifier does not match. Error
  • 405Not POST. Error
  • 500Key creation failed. Error

System

Server health, configuration, and host actions. Configuration is read as JSON with GET /api/config (secrets redacted) and written with POST /config, which merges the posted fields into the stored configuration rather than replacing it.

GET/healthPublic#

Liveness, server version, SSE connection stats and job counts.

Registered without the auth middleware, so it needs no credential even though it reports job counts. Sets fully permissive CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *); OPTIONS answers 200. Paused jobs are counted in jobs.total but in no per-state bucket.

POST/configAdmin#

Merge settings into the configuration, save it and apply it.

Not a full replacement: the server starts from its in-memory configuration and overwrites only the fields below, mostly only when they are present and non-empty (strings) or positive (numbers), so partial posts are safe. Exceptions:

  • dbPath is required on every call.
  • onnxModelPath, onnxLabelsPath, onnxConfigPath and onnxOrtSharedLibPath are assigned unconditionally, so omitting them clears them.
  • Pointer-style fields (transcriptionLanguage, transcriptionVadFilter, transcriptionInitialPrompt, transcriptionHotwords, transcriptionVocalExtract, allowPublicAccess, defaultStartPath) and the arrays byoFaceModels and roots apply whenever present, including empty values; omitted means unchanged.
  • Secret fields equal to <redacted> keep the stored value; storage roots posted with <redacted> credentials recover them from the stored root with the same bucket+endpoint+prefix, else the same label.

Keys not accepted here (for example engines, swipeFeed, reshootModels, dreamModel, autoProcessOps, setupComplete, jwtSecret) are ignored. After saving, the server switches databases if dbPath changed (clearing the auth_token cookie, since users and keys live in the library database), rebuilds the embedding or face index in the background when the active model changed, rebuilds storage backends, and re-applies concurrency caps. A port change takes effect on restart.

Request body

Required, non-blank. A different value switches the library database.

Applied on restart. Out-of-range or 0 is ignored.

POST/Admin#

Legacy single-task job launch.

Queues a one-task workflow. The struct has no JSON tags, so the canonical keys are Command and Arguments; Go's case-insensitive decoding also accepts command and arguments. The last element of Arguments is the task input; the rest are the task's option tokens. Prefer POST /create.

Request body

application/json

Commandstring

Task id.

Argumentsarray of stringrequired

Option tokens followed by the input as the final element.

Example
{
"Command": "metadata",
"Arguments": [
"--type=hash",
"D:\\Media\\clip.mp4"
]
}

Response 201

Queued.

application/json

idstringrequired

Id of the created job (empty string if none was created).

Errors

  • 400bad json, or Arguments empty. Plain text. text/plain
  • 500The workflow could not be queued. Plain text. text/plain

Library Statistics

Library totals and per-metadata-type coverage counts, used by the home page's coverage cards. The counts come from a snapshot, never computed inline in the request: a request that finds the snapshot stale (older than 15 seconds on small libraries, up to 5 minutes on very large ones, scaled by how long the last count took) starts a background recount and is answered from the current snapshot. Running tasks add their completed items on top of the snapshot as they finish, and the merged view is also broadcast over the /stream Server-Sent Events channel as a stats event at most once per second.

GET/api/statsRead#

Library totals and metadata coverage counts.

Serves the latest snapshot with live task progress applied, and starts a background recount when the snapshot is stale. Until the first snapshot after startup (or after a database switch) exists, the response is just {"ready": false}; poll until ready is true.

Coverage counts ignore rows whose media item no longer exists. Transcript coverage is counted against videos and audio only, embedding coverage against the active embedding model, and face-scan coverage against items scanned by any face model. Between recounts, live progress can make a count drift slightly; it never exceeds its denominator.

Response 200

A snapshot, or {"ready": false} before the first count.

application/json

LibraryStats | object

Jobs

Every piece of server work runs as a job in a persistent queue. A job names a task (its command, one of the ids listed by GET /tasks), a list of option tokens (arguments, parsed by the task as --name value or --name=value) and an input string (usually a path, a newline-separated path list, or a query).

Jobs start in pending and are claimed in FIFO order once every job in dependencies has completed and every concurrency bucket the job occupies (host plus resources) has a free slot. A job whose task id is not registered is still accepted; it fails with error when claimed and logs Task not found: <id>.

Live changes to the queue are pushed over GET /stream (create, update, delete, progress and stdout-<jobId> events). Pollers that cannot hold an event stream open can use GET /api/job/{id}.

All routes in this section require an admin credential (bearer JWT, lk_ API key in Authorization or X-API-Key, or the auth_token cookie). Without one, a request that looks like an API call (it sends Accept: application/json, sends a credential header, or its path starts with /api/) gets 401 with the plain-text body Unauthorized; any other request is redirected (302) to /login. While first-run account setup is still pending, a request authenticated as the built-in default admin gets 403 with {"error":"setup_required","message":"Please create a new user account"} (or a redirect to /login?setup=true for browsers).

Most handlers in this section are older ones: their error bodies are plain text (text/plain), not the JSON Error object.

POST/createAdmin#

Create a job from a command string.

Queues one job. The input string is split into tokens by these rules:

  • Tokens are separated by the space character only (tabs and newlines are not separators and stay inside tokens).
  • A double quote (") toggles quoting; spaces inside quotes are kept. The quote characters themselves are removed. There is no escape syntax, so a token cannot contain a literal double quote. Quoting can start mid-token (a"b c"d is one token ab cd).
  • Empty tokens are discarded.

The first token is the task id. If there is more than one token, the last token is the job input and the tokens in between become arguments. A single-token string creates a job with no arguments and an empty input.

Each non-empty key/value pair of fields is then appended to arguments as two tokens, --<key> and <value>, verbatim (no splitting or unquoting), so values can contain spaces, quotes or newlines. Pairs with an empty key or empty value are skipped. Map order is not preserved, and any key is accepted. Task options are parsed with the last occurrence winning, so a fields entry overrides the same option given in input.

The task id is not validated here: an unknown task is accepted and the job fails when it runs. The job is assigned to a fresh single-node workflow (its workflow_id is set).

Request body

application/json

CreateJobRequest

inputstringrequired

Command string: <task-id> [option tokens...] <input>, split on spaces with double-quote grouping (see the operation description).

fieldsmap of string

Extra options appended verbatim as --<key> <value> token pairs. Empty keys or values are skipped.

Example
{
"input": "describe --overwrite \"D:/photos/2024 trip\"",
"fields": {
"prompt": "Describe the scene in one sentence."
}
}

Response 201

Job queued.

application/json

idstringrequired

The new job's id (UUID).

Example
{
"id": "3f0c8f5e-6a0e-4c41-9a7a-2f1f3d0b8c11"
}

Errors

  • 400The body is not valid JSON (bad json) or input contains no tokens (Invalid input). text/plain

POST/job/{id}/cancelAdmin#

Cancel a job.

Cancels a pending, in_progress or paused job: its context is cancelled and its state becomes cancelled immediately. A running task keeps its concurrency slots until it actually returns. Dependents of the job are not cancelled.

The handler ignores the queue's result, so it answers 200 even when the id does not exist or the job is already in a terminal state (nothing changes in those cases).

Workflows

A workflow is a DAG of task nodes (WorkflowTask). Each node becomes one job; a node's dependencies name other nodes in the same DAG, and the job only starts once those jobs have completed.

When a job with dependencies is claimed, its effective input is rebuilt as its original_input followed by, one per line, every output_files entry of each dependency (or, for tasks that register no output files, the dependency's log lines). When a job in a workflow ends in error, every pending job in the same workflow that depends on it (transitively) is cancelled. Cancelling a job by hand does not cascade: its dependents stay pending.

POST /workflow runs an ad-hoc DAG once. Saved workflows (/workflows*) are templates stored in the library database (workflows table, names unique) that can be run any number of times with a runtime input.

All routes require an admin credential; see the Jobs section for how unauthenticated requests are answered. Errors are plain text.

POST/workflowAdmin#

Run a DAG once without saving it.

Queues one job per node, in array order, all sharing a new workflow id. Unlike saved workflows, the DAG is not validated and node ids are used as the job ids verbatim (a node with an empty id gets a generated UUID, but then nothing can depend on it). Node ids must therefore be globally unique across the queue; a clash fails the request part way, leaving earlier nodes queued. A dependency on an id that never becomes a completed job leaves the dependent pending forever.

Request body

application/json

tasksarray of WorkflowTask

The DAG nodes.

Example

"tasks": [
{
"id": "7d9a2a0c-1111-4a5e-9a0b-000000000001",
"command": "metadata",
"arguments": [],
"input": "D:/photos/2024",
"dependencies": []
},
{
"id": "7d9a2a0c-1111-4a5e-9a0b-000000000002",
"command": "autotag",
"arguments": [],
"input": "",
"dependencies": [
"7d9a2a0c-1111-4a5e-9a0b-000000000001"
]
}
]
}

Real-Time Events

GET /stream is a Server-Sent Events feed of queue and library changes, shared by every connected client (there is no per-client filtering). The SPA, the admin pages and the Electron viewer all subscribe to it.

Each message is written as event: <name> and data: <JSON>. The payload shapes are documented as component schemas (JobListEvent, StdoutEvent, ProgressEvent, PeopleUpdatedEvent, DuplicatesUpdatedEvent, MediaPathsEvent, SchedulerEvent, StatsEvent, StreamConnectedEvent).

Delivery is best effort: broadcasts go through a 2048-message hub buffer and a 256-message buffer per client, and a message that does not fit is dropped immediately (counted as dropped_broadcasts / dropped_client_msgs in GET /health). Clients should refetch state after reconnecting rather than rely on replay; there are no event ids and no Last-Event-ID support.

GET/streamPublic#

Server-Sent Events feed of job and library changes.

Opens a text/event-stream (Cache-Control: no-cache, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, never compressed). The route is registered without the auth middleware, so it is open to anyone who can reach the port regardless of the Allow Public Access setting; it carries job metadata and job output lines.

On connect the server first sends one unnamed message (a plain message event) whose data is StreamConnectedEvent. A comment line : keep-alive follows every 30 seconds. Then, for each broadcast, event: <name> plus data: <JSON>:

  • create, update, delete: a job was added (including copies), changed state, or was removed or cleared. Data: JobListEvent. For delete only job.id is meaningful; every other field is a zero value.
  • stdout-<jobId>: one log line from that job. Data: StdoutEvent.
  • progress: item progress of a job (throttled to about 4 per second per job; the first and final updates always go out). Data: ProgressEvent.
  • people-updated: person groupings changed (face clustering finished a model, or a manual People edit). Data: PeopleUpdatedEvent; models is empty for manual edits. Refetch people.
  • duplicates-updated: duplicate-candidate groups changed (the find-duplicates task, or a manual review action). Data: DuplicatesUpdatedEvent; counts are 0 for manual actions. Refetch duplicates.
  • media-updated: the save task overwrote these files in place; bust caches. Data: MediaPathsEvent.
  • media-created: the save task wrote these new files. Data: MediaPathsEvent.
  • scheduler: the auto scheduler changed mode, state, reason or job. Data: SchedulerEvent.
  • stats: library statistics changed (coalesced; at most one per second). Data: StatsEvent, the same object as GET /api/stats.

At most 5000 concurrent connections are accepted. Connections that see no traffic for about two minutes are reaped (keep-alives count as traffic).

Response 200

The event stream. It stays open until the client disconnects or the server shuts down.

text/event-stream

StreamConnectedEvent | JobListEvent | StdoutEvent | ProgressEvent | PeopleUpdatedEvent | DuplicatesUpdatedEvent | MediaPathsEvent | SchedulerEvent | StatsEvent

Server-Sent Events. Each frame carries an event name and one line of JSON data; the data is one of these payloads, chosen by the event name as described above.

Example
data: {"type":"connected","msg":"SSE connection established"}

event: progress
data: {"updateType":"progress","id":"3f0c8f5e-6a0e-4c41-9a7a-2f1f3d0b8c11","done":3,"total":10}

event: stdout-3f0c8f5e-6a0e-4c41-9a7a-2f1f3d0b8c11
data: {"updateType":"stdout","line":"processed D:/photos/a.jpg"}

: keep-alive

Errors

  • 500The response writer cannot stream (Streaming unsupported). text/plain
  • 503The 5000-connection limit is reached (Server at capacity, please try again later). Rejections are counted as rejected_connections in GET /health. text/plain

Media Library

The JSON API the web viewer uses to list, search and edit library items. A media item is identified by its path: an absolute local path or an s3://bucket/key URL inside a configured storage root.

Most of these handlers report errors through a shared helper that writes a JSON body ({"error": "..."}) but with Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8, because it is built on Go's http.Error. Clients should parse the body as JSON regardless of the content type. Those responses are documented here as text/plain with the Error schema.

Several handlers in this section do not check the HTTP method: they decode a JSON body from whatever method is used. The documented method is the one the clients use.

List endpoints (/api/media, /api/media/query, /api/media/search) stream a JSON array of MediaListItem objects in chunks, so a million-item result never sits in server memory. If the database fails after the first chunk has been sent, the connection is aborted instead of ending the array, so a truncated list is never mistaken for a complete one.

With Allow Public Access on, read routes are open to anonymous visitors. Routes that read a file or run ffprobe/ffmpeg on a path then restrict anonymous callers to paths inside a configured storage root or rows already in the library, and never http(s):// URLs; admins are unrestricted.

POST/api/media/queryRead#

Run a composable predicate query, with optional similarity ranking.

The main library query. Predicates are combined left to right: the first predicate with a non-empty value is the base, and each later one is connected to the running result by its own join, or by mode when join is missing or not AND/OR. The expression is parenthesised left-associatively, so a OR b AND c means (a OR b) AND c. Predicates with an empty value are ignored. With no usable predicates the whole library is returned.

The four visual types (similar, visual, clip, face) are resolved through the embedding index into a candidate set of at most 1000 paths, which then takes part in the boolean expression like any other predicate. When every connector is AND and the query mixes visual and non-visual predicates, evaluation is filter-first: the non-visual predicates run first and similarity is scored only inside that set, so the result is the top 1000 most similar items within the filter. If that filter matches nothing, the model is not called at all.

Ordering: - Without a visual predicate the server emits no ORDER BY; the order is whatever SQLite returns (the viewer sorts client side). Every item omits score. - With a visual predicate every item carries score and items are sorted by it, highest first. When several visual predicates match the same item the highest score is kept; items that matched only a non-visual branch of an OR get score 0.

An unknown predicate type produces invalid SQL and a 500.

The handler does not check the method; clients send POST.

Request body

application/json

MediaQueryRequest

modestring

Connector for predicates without their own join. Anything other than exactly OR means AND.

One of "AND" "OR". Default "AND".

predicatesarray of MediaQueryPredicate

Evaluated left to right. Missing or empty returns the whole library.

Example
{
"mode": "AND",
"predicates": [
{
"type": "tag",
"value": "sunset"
},
{
"type": "tag",
"value": "blurry",
"exclude": true
},
{
"type": "path",
"value": "/2024/"
},
{
"type": "orientation",
"value": "landscape",
"join": "OR"
}
]
}

Response 200

Matching items, streamed as one JSON array.

application/json

array of MediaListItem

One item in a list result. Nullable database columns are omitted when NULL (a real zero is still sent).

pathstringrequired

Media path.

mtimeMsintegerrequired

The driving tag assignment's created_at (milliseconds) when a tag predicate drives the row, otherwise 0. Not the file's modification time.

elonumber

Battle Mode rating.

battlesinteger

Battle Mode bout count.

heightinteger

Pixel height.

widthinteger

Pixel width.

weightnumber

Weight of the driving tag assignment.

tagLabelstring

Label of the driving tag assignment.

timeStampnumber

Video timestamp (seconds) of the driving tag assignment.

scorenumber

Similarity score; present on every item, and only then, when the query had a visual predicate.

Example
[
{
"path": "D:/photos/a.jpg",
"mtimeMs": 0,
"elo": 1532.4,
"battles": 7,
"height": 1080,
"width": 1920,
"score": 0.83
},
{
"path": "D:/photos/b.jpg",
"mtimeMs": 0,
"height": 3000,
"width": 2000,
"score": 0.79
}
]

Errors

  • 400The body is not valid JSON. Error
  • 500A similarity search failed (no embedding model, undecodable clip data URL, unknown blend node kind, no face in a face image), or the SQL query failed. Error
POST/api/mediaRead#

List items by tag intersection or union (predecessor of the predicate query).

With an empty or missing tags array, returns every item in the library ordered by path (tag fields are empty strings and 0).

With tags, mode (case-insensitive, default EXCLUSIVE) chooses the semantics: - EXCLUSIVE: items that carry every listed tag, one row per item, ordered by path. The tag fields come from one of the item's matching assignments. - Any other value: one row per matching tag assignment, ordered by path. An item carrying two of the tags, or one tag at several video timestamps, appears more than once.

Only POST is handled. Any other method gets an empty 200 response with no body.

tagsarray of string

modestring

Items visually similar to a library item.

Ranks the library by cosine similarity to the item's embedding in the active embedding model. When the item has no stored vector it is embedded on the fly (and the vector is saved). The item itself is usually the top hit.

The handler does not check the method.

POST/api/media/search/faceRead#

Find media containing the person whose face is in an uploaded image.

The request body is the raw bytes of an image. Faces are detected in it and matched against stored face embeddings. limit counts faces searched; hits are then collapsed to one item per media path (best face wins), so the result can hold fewer items than limit.

Number of face hits to search. Non-positive or invalid values use the default; values above 500 are capped to 500.

POST/api/media/previewRead#

Server-side path of an item's thumbnail, generating it if missing.

Returns the thumbnail's location as a JSON string: a local filesystem path on the server, or an s3:// URL for media in a bucket. To fetch the image bytes use GET /media/thumbnail instead.

Lookup order: the path recorded in the item's thumbnail column (if the file or object still exists), then for local media the deterministic cache path on disk, then generation (throttled). Results are written back to the item's row.

The handler does not check the method; clients send POST.

POST/api/media/battleAdmin#

Record a Battle Mode vote and update both Elo ratings.

The Elo math runs server side in one transaction, and the vote is appended to the battle log. Ratings start at 1500. The K-factor depends on how many battles the item has fought: 48 under 10, 24 under 30, 12 after that. A win adds 1 to the winner's wins and the loser's losses; a draw changes neither. battles is reset from the battle-log count. A path with no library row gets one created.

Path of the item that won.

loserPathstringrequired

Path of the item that lost. Must differ from winnerPath.

The winner's score. 1 is a win, 0.5 a draw.

One of 1 0.5. Default 1.

Example

"winnerPath": "D:/photos/a.jpg",
"loserPath": "D:/photos/b.jpg"
}

Response 200

The new ratings and battle counts.

winnerPathstringrequired
winnerElonumberrequired

Winner's rating after the vote.

winnerMatchesintegerrequired

Winner's battle count including this one.

loserPathstringrequired
loserElonumberrequired
loserMatchesintegerrequired
Example
{
"winnerPath": "D:/photos/a.jpg",
"winnerElo": 1524,
"winnerMatches": 1,
"loserPath": "D:/photos/b.jpg",
"loserElo": 1476,

POST/api/media/moveAdmin#

Re-point every database reference after moving a file or folder on disk.

The bookkeeping half of a move: the filesystem is never touched, the caller has already moved the file(s). All references are rewritten in one transaction: media.path, media_tag_by_category.media_path, media_embedding.media_path, face.media_path, face_scan.media_path, battle.winner_path, battle.loser_path, duplicate_member.media_path and duplicate_group.anchor_path. Tables that do not exist in the library are skipped (their key is absent from rows).

from and to are trimmed of whitespace and trailing / or \. With prefix, both are folders and every item under from moves under to keeping its sub-path. Matching is segment-aligned (/a/foo never drags /a/foobar) and case-sensitive.

With dryRun the whole move runs and is rolled back, so the counts are exactly what a real run would change.

If any destination path already belongs to another library item that is not itself moving, nothing changes and the answer is 409. This check also applies to dry runs.

After a real move the vector and face indexes are re-keyed for the paths listed in paths. When truncated is true only the first 100 were re-keyed; rebuild the index to refresh the rest.

The handler does not check the method; clients send POST.

Request body

application/json

fromstringrequired

Current path (or folder with prefix). Required.

tostringrequired

New path (or folder with prefix). Required, must differ from from, and with prefix must not be inside from.

prefixboolean

Treat from and to as folders and move the whole subtree.

Default false.

dryRunboolean

Compute the result and roll back.

Default false.

Example
{
"from": "C:/pics/2023",
"to": "D:/archive/2023",
"prefix": true,
"dryRun": true
}

Response 200

What the move changed (or would change, for a dry run).

application/json

MediaMoveResult

fromstringrequired

Normalised source (trimmed of whitespace and trailing separators).

tostringrequired

Normalised destination.

prefixbooleanrequired
dryRunbooleanrequired
itemsintegerrequired

Number of media rows whose path changed.

rowsmap of integerrequired

Rows updated per table.column key (for example media.path, media_tag_by_category.media_path), including zero entries. Tables missing from the library have no key.

totalintegerrequired

Sum of rows.

pathsarray of object

Up to 100 sample rewrites, ordered by old path. Omitted when nothing matched.

fromstringrequired
tostringrequired
truncatedboolean

True when more than 100 items moved; omitted otherwise.

Example
{
"from": "C:/pics/2023",
"to": "D:/archive/2023",
"prefix": true,
"dryRun": true,
"items": 2,
"rows": {
"media.path": 2,
"media_tag_by_category.media_path": 9,
"media_embedding.media_path": 2,
"face.media_path": 1,
"face_scan.media_path": 2,
"battle.winner_path": 0,
"battle.loser_path": 0,
"duplicate_member.media_path": 0,
"duplicate_group.anchor_path": 0
},
"total": 16,
"paths": [
{
"from": "C:/pics/2023/a.jpg",
"to": "D:/archive/2023/a.jpg"
},
{
"from": "C:/pics/2023/b.jpg",
"to": "D:/archive/2023/b.jpg"
}
]
}

Errors

  • 400Invalid JSON, from or to empty, both the same, to inside from with prefix, or a database error during the move. Error
  • 409One or more destination paths already belong to another library item. Nothing was changed. Unlike the other errors, this body is sent as application/json. application/json
POST/api/media/merge-metadataAdmin#

Merge several items into the first one, then delete the others.

The first non-blank path is the target; every other distinct path is a source. The merge is additive: tag rows and per-model embedding rows the target lacks are copied in (the target's own rows win), an empty transcript is filled from the first source that has one, and that source's .vtt sidecar is moved next to the target. The sources are then deleted from disk (plus leftover sidecars) and every database reference to them is erased. s3:// sources and files that fail to delete keep their file and rows and are listed in failed.

The handler does not check the method; clients send POST.

Request body

application/json

pathsarray of stringrequired

Target first, then the sources. Blank entries and repeats of the target are skipped.

Example
{
"paths": [
"D:/photos/keep.jpg",
"D:/photos/dupe1.jpg",
"D:/photos/dupe2.jpg"
]
}

Response 200

What the merge changed.

application/json

MediaMergeResult

targetstringrequired
sourcesarray of stringrequired
tagsintegerrequired

Tag rows the target gained.

embeddingsintegerrequired

POST/api/media/assign-personAdmin#

Assign a face in a media item to a person, or found a new person from it.

Assigns one face of the item: when the item has several faces, the one most similar to the person's existing faces wins; for a person with no faces yet (always the case with newPerson) the largest face wins. The item is face-scanned on the fly when it has no stored faces yet.

With newPerson: true a new person is created (named name, or the next automatic "Unknown" name) only after a face has been found, so a face-less item never leaves an empty group behind; setCover is then implied. The assignment is recorded as a user action.

Request body

application/json

pathstringrequired

Media path. Required.

personIdinteger

Existing person id. Required unless newPerson is true.

setCoverboolean

Also make the chosen face the person's cover crop.

Default false.

newPersonboolean

Create a new person seeded by this item's face.

Default false.

namestring

Name for the new person (with newPerson). Blank picks an automatic name.

Example
{
"path": "D:/photos/x.jpg",
"personId": 12,
"setCover": true
}

Response 200

The face that was assigned.

application/json

faceIdintegerrequired

Id of the assigned face.

personIdintegerrequired

The person it was assigned to (the new id with newPerson).

facesintegerrequired

Number of faces found in the item.

setCoverbooleanrequired

Whether the face became the cover.

createdbooleanrequired

True when a new person was created.

namestringrequired

The new person's name; empty when assigning to an existing person.

Example
{
"faceId": 4411,
"personId": 31,
"faces": 2,
"setCover": true,
"created": true,
"name": "Alex"
}

Errors

  • 400Invalid JSON, path empty, or neither a positive personId nor newPerson; also person-creation or assignment errors whose message says something is already so, required, or must be. Error
  • 404personId does not exist. Error
  • 405The method is not POST. Error
  • 422No face was detected in the media item. Error
  • 500Face scan or database failure. Error

Reject every face of a person on one media item.

The inverse of assign-person: each of the person's faces on the item gets a permanent veto plus cannot-links and is unassigned, so the group actually loses those faces. Used by the Electron viewer when a person tag is removed from an item. The person is identified by personId, or by display name when personId is missing or not positive.

File Serving

Byte-serving endpoints for media files, thumbnails, HLS renditions and face crops. These are plain GET URLs meant to be used directly in <img>, <video> and HLS players.

The path query parameter of /media/file and /media/thumbnail is read from the raw query string and decoded with path-unescaping, so a + stays a literal plus sign (encode spaces as %20). Only the first path= occurrence is used.

Local files are served by Go's http.ServeFile, which supports Range requests (206 Partial Content) and If-Modified-Since. Files in an S3-compatible root are not proxied: the server answers 302 Found with a presigned URL.

For anonymous callers under Allow Public Access, paths outside every configured storage root are refused with 403.

GET/media/fileRead#

Serve a media file.

  • Local files stream through http.ServeFile with Range support, no size limit, Content-Type from the extension (unknown extensions are application/octet-stream), Content-Length, Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 and an ETag of the form "<name>-<size>-<mtime>". A matching If-None-Match answers 304.
  • HEIC/HEIF files, which browsers cannot decode, are served as a cached JPEG rendering instead.
  • s3:// paths answer 302 to a presigned URL.
  • http(s):// paths (admins only) are proxied through an SSRF-safe client: only the remote Content-Type, Content-Length, Cache-Control and ETag are copied (default Cache-Control: public, max-age=1800), and bodies are cut at 100 MB.

Query parameters

pathstringrequired

Absolute local path, s3:// URL, or http(s):// URL. Percent-encode it; + is not decoded as a space.

Headers

Rangestring

Byte range, for local files.

If-None-Matchstring

An ETag from a previous response.

Response 200

The file bytes.

application/octet-stream

string (binary)

image/*

string (binary)

video/*

string (binary)

audio/*

string (binary)

Response 206

Partial content for a Range request.

application/octet-stream

string (binary)

Response 302

s3:// path: redirect to a presigned URL.

Response 304

If-None-Match matched the current ETag.

Errors

  • 400path missing, empty or badly encoded, a local path that is not absolute, a directory, or an invalid remote URL. text/plain
  • 403Anonymous caller and the path is outside every storage root and not a library row, or is an http(s):// URL. text/plain
  • 404Local file not found, or no storage backend for the s3:// path. text/plain
  • 405The method is not GET. text/plain
  • 413Remote (http(s)://) file larger than 100 MB according to its Content-Length. text/plain
  • 415HEIC conversion failed. text/plain
  • 500The file could not be stat'ed, or a presigned URL could not be generated. text/plain
  • 502The remote URL could not be fetched. A remote non-200 status is passed through with a plain-text body. text/plain
GET/media/thumbnailRead#

Serve a thumbnail image, generating it on first request.

Lookup order: a thumbnail recorded in the item's cache column (an existing s3:// object is answered with a 302 to a presigned URL), then for s3:// media generation into the bucket followed by a 302, then for local media the recorded file, the deterministic cache path, and finally generation (throttled). Generated paths are stored on the item's row.

Local thumbnails are sent with Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, immutable and an ETag of "<file name>-<size>"; a matching If-None-Match answers 304, and Range is supported. Video thumbnails are short .mp4 clips (video/mp4). Image thumbnails are PNG data in extensionless files, so they are labelled application/octet-stream.

Query parameters

pathstringrequired

Media path (absolute local path or s3:// URL). Read from the raw query string like /media/file.

cacheThumbnailCache

Thumbnail size column. Any other value means thumbnail_path_600.

One of "thumbnail_path_100" "thumbnail_path_600" "thumbnail_path_1200".

tsnumber

Video frame time in seconds. Invalid values are ignored. A non-zero value gets its own cache file.

Default 0.

Headers

If-None-Matchstring

Response 200

Thumbnail bytes.

application/octet-stream

string (binary)

video/mp4

string (binary)

Response 302

S3 media or an S3 thumbnail; redirect to a presigned URL.

Response 304

If-None-Match matched.

Errors

  • 400path missing, empty or badly encoded, or an s3:// path whose root is not S3 storage. text/plain
  • 403Anonymous caller and the local path is outside every configured storage root. (Unlike /media/file, a library row outside the roots is not enough.) text/plain
  • 404Source file not found, or no storage backend for the s3:// path. text/plain
  • 405The method is not GET. text/plain
  • 500No database configured, generation failed, or a presigned URL could not be generated. text/plain
GET/media/hlsRead#

HLS rendition status for a video, starting the transcode if needed.

Renditions are a stream-copy (no re-encode) VOD HLS stream with 6-second MPEG-TS segments, cached under the server's data directory keyed by the SHA-256 of path. One ffmpeg runs at a time; other requests queue.

Without check=true, a video that is neither cached nor in progress starts generating and the response is processing with the probed duration. Poll until ready, then load url in an HLS player. A failed generation is reported once as error and its partial output removed; the next request starts again.

Responses carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

Query parameters

pathstringrequired

Media path of the video.

checkstring

true reports idle instead of starting a transcode when nothing is cached.

One of "true".

Response 200

Current status.

application/json

HlsStatus

statusstringrequired

queued = waiting for the single ffmpeg slot; idle = nothing cached and check=true.

One of "ready" "processing" "queued" "idle" "error".

urlstring

Master playlist URL, when ready.

progressnumber

Fraction done while processing; omitted when 0.

min 0, max 1.

durationnumber

Source duration in seconds; only on the response that starts generation.

errorstring

Failure message, when error.

Example
{
"status": "ready",
"url": "/media/hls/6f1c...9a/master.m3u8"
}

Errors

  • 400path is missing. text/plain
  • 403Anonymous caller and the path is outside every configured storage root. text/plain
  • 405Method other than GET or DELETE. text/plain
DELETE/media/hlsAdmin#

Delete cached HLS renditions.

With path, removes that video's renditions; without it, removes the entire HLS cache. The route is read, but this method always needs admin credentials when Allow Public Access is on (anonymous callers get 401 JSON).

Query parameters

pathstring

Media path whose renditions to delete. Omit to clear everything.

Response 204

Deleted (also when nothing was cached).

Errors

  • 401Allow Public Access is on and the caller is not an admin. Error

Serve a top-level HLS playlist from the cache.

Served by the /media/hls/ prefix route. {hash} is the cache key from the url returned by GET /media/hls. The file must match master.m3u8 or stream.m3u8 at this level (segment names pass validation too, but are served with the playlist content type). Supports Range; carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

Path parameters

Lowercase hex cache key.

filestringrequired

master.m3u8 or stream.m3u8.

Response 200

The playlist.

application/vnd.apple.mpegurl

string

Errors

  • 400Invalid hash or file name, or a path with the wrong number of segments. text/plain
  • 404Not in the cache. text/plain
GET/media/hls/{hash}/{preset}/{file}Read#

Serve a rendition playlist or segment from the cache.

Served by the /media/hls/ prefix route. Normally reached through the master playlist. The server currently only generates the passthrough preset. .ts files are sent as video/MP2T, playlists as application/vnd.apple.mpegurl. Supports Range; carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

Path parameters

Response 200

video/MP2T

Errors

  • 400Invalid hash, preset or file name. text/plain

GET/media/facecropRead#

JPEG crop of one detected face.

Decodes the face's source media (for a video, the same midpoint frame the face scan used; the stored 600 px thumbnail is a last resort), cuts out the face box with a 35% margin, and scales it so the longer edge is size. Sent with Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400 (a face id's crop never changes; rescans mint new ids). JPEG quality 88.

Query parameters

idintegerrequired

Face id.

sizeinteger

Longer edge in pixels. Values outside 32 to 1024, or not a number, use the default.

Default 160. min 32, max 1024.

Response 200

The crop.

image/jpeg

string (binary)

Errors

  • 400id missing or not an integer. Error
  • 403Anonymous caller and the face's media is outside every storage root and not a library row. Error
  • 404No face with this id, or its media (and thumbnail) cannot be decoded. Error
  • 405The method is not GET. Error
  • 500The database failed. Error

Taxonomy

A category groups tags. An assignment attaches a tag to a media item, optionally at a video timestamp (0 means untimed) and with a weight used for ordering. Tag labels are unique across the library and each tag belongs to one category. An assignment's category always mirrors its tag's category.

Read endpoints are read access. Every mutation is admin.

Most handlers in this section do not check the HTTP method: they accept any method with the documented body, and the method shown is the one the web client sends. The exceptions are the method-dispatching paths (/api/tags, /api/tags/timestamp, /api/categories, /api/assignments), which act only on the listed methods and answer any other method with an empty 200, and GET /api/tags/list, which returns 405 for other methods.

Errors from these handlers carry a JSON body {"error": "..."} but are sent with Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8. Mutations return {} on success unless noted.

GET/api/taxonomyRead#

Every category with all of its tags.

Returns an object keyed by category label (not an array), in the same shape as the desktop app's taxonomy. Keys are inserted in category weight order, and each category's tags are ordered by tag weight. On large libraries this is a big payload; the web client loads /api/taxonomy/categories and then /api/taxonomy/tags?category= per category instead. The method is not checked.

Response 200

Map of category label to category.

application/json

map of TaxonomyCategory

Example
{
"People": {
"label": "People",
"weight": 0,
"tagViewMode": "card",
"tags": [
{
"label": "Alice",
"category": "People",
"weight": 0
},
{
"label": "Bob",
"category": "People",
"weight": 1
}
]
},
"Places": {
"label": "Places",
"weight": 1,
"tagViewMode": "list",
"tags": []
}
}

Errors

  • 500Database error. Error

Delete a category with its tags, tag groups and their assignments.

Removes, in one transaction, the assignments of every tag filed under the category (plus leftover assignments labelled with the category whose tag no longer exists, but never assignments of a tag that now lives in another category), the tags, the category's tag groups and the category itself. Responds with what was removed, counted inside the same transaction; GET /api/categories/impact returns the same numbers without deleting. Deleting a category that does not exist succeeds with exists: false and zero counts.

Request body

application/json

labelstringrequired

Category to delete.

Example
{
"label": "Suggested"
}

Response 200

Deleted; what was removed.

application/json

CategoryImpact

labelstringrequired
existsbooleanrequired

Whether the category exists.

tagsintegerrequired

Tags filed under the category.

groupsintegerrequired

Tag groups in the category.

assignmentsintegerrequired

Assignment rows removed with them.

mediaintegerrequired

Distinct media items those assignments are on.

Example
{
"label": "Suggested",
"exists": true,
"tags": 1800,
"groups": 0,
"assignments": 92000,
"media": 41000
}

Errors

  • 400Body is not valid JSON or label is empty. Error
  • 409Unique-constraint conflict; nothing changed. Error
  • 500Database error; nothing changed. Error

POST/api/assignmentsAdmin#

Tag one or many media items.

  • mediaPaths takes precedence; mediaPath is used only when mediaPaths is empty.
  • The assignment is always filed under the tag's own category. Naming a different category than the tag's is a 409.
  • A tag that does not exist yet is created at the end of categoryLabel, which must name an existing category (400 otherwise, or when categoryLabel is omitted).
  • Existing identical assignments (same path, tag and timestamp) are left alone. New ones get ascending weights after the tag's current assignment count.
  • With applyTagPreview, the first item's 600px thumbnail (generated if needed) becomes the tag's preview image. A thumbnail failure is only logged.

Request body

application/json

mediaPathsarray of string

Items to tag. One of mediaPaths or mediaPath is required.

mediaPathstring

Single item to tag, used when mediaPaths is empty.

tagLabelstringrequired

Tag to assign.

categoryLabelstring

The tag's category. Required only when the tag does not exist yet.

timeStampnumber

Video time in seconds. Default 0 (untimed).

applyTagPreviewboolean

Make the first item the tag's preview image. Default false.

Example
{
"mediaPaths": [
"D:\\Photos\\a.jpg",
"D:\\Photos\\b.jpg"
],
"tagLabel": "Alice",
"categoryLabel": "People"
}

Response 200

Assigned.

application/json

EmptyObject

Errors

  • 500Database error; nothing was assigned. Error
DELETE/api/assignmentsAdmin#

Remove a tag from one or many media items.

  • mediaPaths takes precedence over mediaPath.
  • A non-zero tag.time_stamp removes only the assignment at that time. A time_stamp of 0 (or omitted) removes every assignment of the tag on the item, timed or not.
  • If the tag is a person's name and an item no longer carries it at any timestamp, that person's faces on the item are rejected (vetoed) so clustering cannot put them back.
  • Nothing is validated and database errors are not reported.

Tag Groups

Tag groups are a purely visual level between a category and its tags: a group is identified by its category and label, and a tag carries at most one group label. Search and query paths ignore groups. A tag leaves its group when it moves to another category, and deleting a group never deletes its tags (they become ungrouped). A category with tag grouping turned off lists its tags flat.

As in Taxonomy, these handlers do not check the method (except the method-dispatching /api/tag-groups), and errors are JSON {"error": "..."} sent as text/plain.

A category's tag groups in order.

Ordered by weight, then label. Without category the result is an empty array. The method is not checked.

array of TagGroup

labelstringrequired
weightnumberrequired

hiddenbooleanrequired

Left out of the taxonomy panel unless hidden groups are shown.

viewModestring | nullrequired

One of "card" "list" null.

"weight": 1,
"hidden": false,
"viewMode": null
},
{
"label": "Work",
"weight": 2,
"hidden": true,
"viewMode": "list"
}
]

Errors

Embeddings Index

Vectors are stored per model in the media_embedding table and loaded into an exact in-memory cosine index for the active embedding model at startup and after each embed job. These endpoints inspect and maintain both. All are admin and enforce their HTTP method (405 otherwise). Errors are JSON {"error": "..."} sent as text/plain.

Response 200

People and Faces

A face is one detection with an identity embedding, stored per media item by the face-scan task. A person is a cluster of faces, either named or auto-named Unknown #N; each person is also a tag in the People category, so person names work in library search, and rename, merge and delete cascade to those tag rows.

A face is assigned either by clustering (assignedBy: auto) or by hand (user). User assignments, rejections (vetoes and cannot-links) and group bans are permanent across re-clustering: locking or curating a group is how you make the clusterer's result stick. Grouping strictness is set with /api/faces/tuning.

Every manual change here broadcasts a people-updated event on /stream. Face crops are served by /media/facecrop?id=.

Most error bodies in this section are {"error": "..."} sent with Content-Type: text/plain.

GET/api/peopleRead#

List every person.

Returns every person with face and media counts, most faces first. Always an array (empty when there are no people).

Response 200

All people.

application/json

array of Person

A named (or auto-named Unknown #N) cluster of faces. Every person has a name so it can live in the taxonomy as a People-category tag.

idinteger (int64)required
namestringrequired

Stored name. May end in _cluster when a tag in another category owns the plain name; UIs strip the suffix for display.

coverFaceIdinteger (int64)

Face used as the preview crop (/media/facecrop?id=): the chosen cover when it still belongs to the person, else the best face (confidence times bbox area). Omitted when the person has no faces.

faceCountintegerrequired

Faces assigned to the person.

mediaCountintegerrequired

Distinct media items containing the person.

lockedCountintegerrequired

Faces that are user assignments (confirmed); these survive every recluster.

createdAtinteger (int64)

Unix seconds. Omitted when unknown.

modelsstring

Comma-separated recognizer id(s) of the person's faces (normally one, e.g. anime-ccip for a drawn-character cluster). Omitted when the person has no faces.

Example
[
{
"id": 12,
"name": "Ada",
"coverFaceId": 4031,
"faceCount": 87,
"mediaCount": 64,
"lockedCount": 20,
"createdAt": 1761900000,
"models": "buffalo_l"
},
{
"id": 13,
"name": "Unknown #4",
"faceCount": 6,
"mediaCount": 6,
"lockedCount": 0,
"createdAt": 1761900500,
"models": "buffalo_l"
}
]

Errors

  • 405Method other than GET or POST. The body is {"error": "..."} but is sent with Content-Type: text/plain. Error
  • 500Database or internal failure. The body is {"error": "..."} but is sent with Content-Type: text/plain. Error
POST/api/peopleAdmin#

Create an empty named person.

The route is registered read-level, so the write is re-checked: while Allow Public Access is on an admin credential is required (401 JSON otherwise). With public access off the normal login requirement already applies. Broadcasts a people-updated event on /stream.

Request body

application/json

namestringrequired

Person name; trimmed. Must be non-empty and not already used by another person.

Example

"name": "Ada"
}

Response 200

Created.

application/json

idinteger (int64)required

New person id.

namestringrequired

The trimmed requested name. The stored name may carry a _cluster suffix when a non-People tag already owns the plain name; this field does not reflect that.

Example

"id": 14,
"name": "Ada"
}

Errors

  • 400Body is not valid JSON, the name is empty, or a person with that name already exists. The body is {"error": "..."} but is sent with Content-Type: text/plain. Error
  • 401Allow Public Access is on and the request carries no admin credential (anonymous visitors may read but not write here). Error
  • 500Database or internal failure. The body is {"error": "..."} but is sent with Content-Type: text/plain. Error
POST/api/people/lock-allAdmin#

Confirm every auto-assigned face of every named person.

Promotes every auto-assigned face of every NAMED person to a user assignment. Auto-named Unknown #N clusters are skipped. Locked faces survive every regroup. Broadcasts people-updated only when at least one face was locked. No request body.

Response 200

Counts.

application/json

peopleintegerrequired

lockedintegerrequired

Faces promoted to user assignments.

Example

"people": 9,
"locked": 412
}

Errors

  • 500Database or internal failure. The body is {"error": "..."} but is sent with Content-Type: text/plain. Error
DELETE/api/people/{id}Admin#

Delete a person.

Removes the person and their People-category tag rows. By default the faces are kept (unassigned, free to re-cluster) and the dissolved membership is recorded as a group ban so the same group does not simply re-form on the next clustering pass.

  • deleteFaces=true deletes the face rows too (and drops them from the search index); they stay gone until their media is rescanned. No ban is recorded in this mode.
  • ban=false skips recording the ban.

Only DELETE is accepted on this path. Broadcasts a people-updated event on /stream.

Path parameters

idinteger (int64)required

Person id (positive integer).

min 1.

Query parameters

deleteFacesstring

Exactly true also deletes the person's faces. Any other value is ignored.

One of "true".

banstring

Exactly false skips recording the group ban. Ignored when deleteFaces=true.

One of "false".

Response 200

Deleted. With deleteFaces=true the body is {deleted, facesDeleted}; otherwise {deleted, banned}.

application/json

object | object

Example
{
"deleted": 13,
"banned": 6
}

Errors

  • 400Invalid person id. The body is {"error": "..."} but is sent with Content-Type: text/plain. Error
  • 404No person with that id. The body is {"error": "..."} but is sent with Content-Type: text/plain. Error
  • 405Method other than DELETE. The body is {"error": "..."} but is sent with Content-Type: text/plain. Error
  • 500Database or internal failure. The body is {"error": "..."} but is sent with Content-Type: text/plain. Error

  • 500Saving the config failed. The body is {"error": "..."} but is sent with Content-Type: text/plain. Error

Duplicate Candidates

A duplicate group is a cluster of media whose visual embeddings are at least a threshold similar to the group's anchor item. Groups are stars around the anchor, not chains, and a media path belongs to at most one group. They are produced by the review-only find-duplicates task (unlike the exact-bytes dedupe task, it never merges or deletes) and reviewed here: merge the copies, dismiss look-alikes, or exclude a single member. The merge-duplicates task is the bulk accept.

A dismissed group, and an excluded member, keep their rows so later scans do not regroup them. Removing or merging media removes its member rows; a group left with fewer than two members is pruned, and one whose anchor is gone is re-anchored on its best remaining member. The dupe: query predicate filters the library to group members.

Every write here broadcasts duplicates-updated on /stream. Error bodies are {"error": "..."} sent with Content-Type: text/plain.

Default 50. min 1, max 500.

Default 0. min 0.

Response 200

application/json

totalintegerrequired

POST/api/duplicates/{id}/mergeAdmin#

Merge group members into one keeper.

Runs the same merge as POST /api/media/merge-metadata: the keeper gains the sources' tags, embeddings and transcript, and the sources are deleted from disk and the database (s3:// sources and files that fail to delete are reported in failed and keep their rows). Member rows follow the deletions, so a fully merged group disappears and a partially merged one stays pending with what is left.

  • keep defaults to the group's keeperPath (highest resolution, then largest file, then the anchor). It must be a member.
  • sources defaults to every other active member. Excluded members are merged only when named. Blank entries and the keeper itself are skipped.

Also broadcasts people-updated when merged sources had faces. Broadcasts a duplicates-updated event on /stream.

Path parameters

idinteger (int64)required

Group id (positive integer).

min 1.

application/json

keepstring

Path of the member to keep.

]

Mark a group as not duplicates.

Sets the status to dismissed. The members keep their rows, so they are never regrouped by later scans. No request body. Broadcasts a duplicates-updated event on /stream.

POST/api/duplicates/{id}/excludeAdmin#

Pull one member out of a group, or put it back.

An excluded member keeps its row (so it is never regrouped with the same partners) but is never merged by default. When fewer than two active members remain the group is dismissed automatically; when the anchor is excluded the group is re-anchored on an active member. Broadcasts a duplicates-updated event on /stream.

Swipe

Swipe is a mobile-first progressive web app served at /swipe for flicking through the library one item at a time. /swipe/api feeds it pages of items in several modes (shuffle, more like this, a personalized For You feed, text search, same person), and /swipe/manifest.json makes it installable. Errors from /swipe/api are plain-text messages.

GET/swipe/apiRead#

A page of items for the Swipe app.

The mode parameter picks how items are chosen. Any other value (or none) uses the shuffle.

  • Omitted: shuffle. With no q, a seeded sample of the whole library (seed 0 or omitted means fresh randomness). With q, the library search query filters the pool: pure tag queries (tag:"X", OR/AND of tags) shuffle with seed; other queries are ordered by SQL RANDOM() on every request, so their pages are not stable.
  • similar: ranked by visual-embedding similarity to anchor (active embedding model), nearest first.
  • feed: the personalized "For You" feed built from the user's swipe favorites (the tag configured in the swipeFeed config section). The server keeps one feed sequence per session (and per orientation) so pages compose. exploit, fresh, bridge and wildcard override the configured lane weights for this request.
  • text: the library ranked by SigLIP text-to-image similarity to q (required). Query vectors are cached for 15 minutes so paging does not re-encode.
  • face: ranked by face similarity to the largest face in anchor (scanned on the fly when it has no stored faces), one entry per media item.

In similar, text and face modes the ranking is deterministic, the anchor is excluded, and missing-media and off-orientation items are filtered before paging, so offsets index a stable list.

Query parameters

modestring

Selection mode; see the description. Unrecognized values fall back to the shuffle.

One of "similar" "feed" "text" "face".

qstring

Shuffle mode: library search query filter. text mode: the search text (required, trimmed).

anchorstring

Media path. Required for similar and face; excluded from its own results.

seedinteger (int64)

Shuffle mode only. Same seed, same order (for unfiltered and tag-filtered pools). 0 means fresh randomness.

Default 0.

sessionstring

feed mode: client session id keying the server-side feed sequence.

Default "default".

exploitnumber

feed mode: weight override for the nearest-neighbours-of-your-taste lane. Must be >= 0.

min 0.

freshnumber

feed mode: weight override for the neighbours-of-the-latest-like lane. Must be >= 0.

min 0.

bridgenumber

feed mode: weight override for the between-interests "surprising" lane. Must be >= 0.

min 0.

wildcardnumber

feed mode: weight override for the uniform-random lane. Must be >= 0.

min 0.

orientationstring

Restrict to portrait (width <= height) or landscape (width >= height); items without dimensions are excluded when set. Any other value (including both) means unrestricted. Case-insensitive.

One of "portrait" "landscape".

offsetinteger

Page offset.

Default 0. min 0.

limitinteger

Page size. Values outside 1-50 use the default.

Default 20. min 1, max 50.

Response 200

One page of items.

application/json

SwipeResponse

itemsarray | nullrequired

The page. The shuffle mode returns null (not an empty array) when the pool is empty.

has_morebooleanrequired

More items exist past this page.

total_countintegerrequired

Not populated by this endpoint; always 0.

Example
{
"items": [
{
"path": "D:/photos/beach.jpg",
"description": "A beach at sunset.",
"size": 2483112,
"hash": "a1b2c3",
"width": 4032,
"height": 3024,
"tags": [
{
"label": "beach",
"category": "Places"
}
],
"exists": true,
"duplicateCount": 0
}
],
"has_more": true,
"total_count": 0
}

Errors

  • 400anchor missing for similar/face, or q empty for text. Plain-text message. text/plain
  • 405Method other than GET (Use GET). text/plain
  • 500Search, feed or database failure, including no face found in the face anchor and the text model not being installed. Plain-text message. text/plain
